ranking_stability.status: PROJECTION, not a measurement. See the assumptions below
ranking_stability.why_it_matters: the Danish half of every score is final, because CORDIS is complete. The AU half rests on the covered papers only, so the ranking will move when the rest of the lookup lands
ranking_stability.coverage_spread_note: departments are not currently comparable with each other. Coverage runs from 53.9 percent to 94.8 percent across the departments in this list, so a department whose papers happened to fall in the covered slice looks stronger than one whose papers did not, for no reason connected to its research
assumptions: a company co-author is equally likely on any paper, which is false: some topics are far more industry-facing than others
the covered papers are a random sample of each department's output, which is false: they are heavy with one publication year

loose_cordis_tags.what_this_measures: a link can be produced by a correct bridge from a loose tag. A CORDIS project tagged with one euroSciVoc term uses that word with nothing to corroborate it, and some of those words are homonyms. An organisation is counted weakly supported on a topic when no project connecting it to that topic carries a second euroSciVoc term from the same domain as the term that carried the topic
loose_cordis_tags.why_not_the_simpler_test: asking whether the project's OTHER terms sit in a different domain misses the worst cases, because the worst projects have no other terms at all. The project that exposed this, Novo Nordisk under Ecology, carries exactly one term
loose_cordis_tags.what_this_test_misses: corroboration is checked at the euroSciVoc DOMAIN level, which is coarse, so a loose tag sitting beside an unrelated term from the same broad domain passes. Region Hovedstaden reaches Ecology partly through project 101137378, a psilocybin trial in palliative care, whose terms are ecosystems, neurobiology, multiple sclerosis and anxiety disorders. Ecosystems and neurobiology are both natural sciences, and both are still biological sciences one level down, so no level of this test catches it. Tightening the test to the next level down flags 63 percent of listed organisations instead of 25 and still misses that case, so the conservative version is kept and this number is a floor on the problem, not a measure of it.
loose_cordis_tags.a_named_case_the_test_correctly_clears: Region Hovedstaden also reaches Ecology through project 101112723, on remediation and restoration of contaminated land, which is a genuinely ecological link. A health region under Ecology looks wrong and is not always wrong
loose_cordis_tags.not_a_wrongness_measure: weak support is not the same as a wrong link. Blue World Technologies reaches Organic Chemistry through the term alcohols on a bio-methanol project, which is uncorroborated and entirely correct

verdicts._what_this_is: Hand verdicts on the 20 topic assignments sampled in data/derived/topic_check_sample.json, seed 20260914. Judged by reading each row, not by any rule. 'right' means the assigned topic describes the paper or the term. 'partly right' means it is in the right area but loses or bends the meaning. 'wrong' means it would mislead someone reading the Action. Ten rows test the paper to subfield step, which is OpenAlex's work; ten test the euroSciVoc term to subfield bridge, which is this project's work.

s01.note: A paper titled Computational Chemistry is assigned the topic Mass Spectrometry Techniques and Applications and so the subfield Spectroscopy. Computational chemistry is not spectroscopy. The paper to topic step misfired, probably on a short and generic title.

s02.note: A paper on solar variability from radiocarbon records lands in the subfield Molecular Biology. The paper to topic step is fine, Geomagnetism and Paleomagnetism Studies is a fair topic for it. The error is in OpenAlex's own hierarchy: that topic is filed under subfield Molecular Biology, field Biochemistry Genetics and Molecular Biology. Checked against the cached OpenAlex topic list, so this is upstream and not a fault of this pipeline.

s03.note: A diatom peptide used to fabricate titanium dioxide nanosheets, assigned Biomaterials. The topic Diatoms and Algae Research sits under Biomaterials in OpenAlex, which is odd in general, but for this particular paper Biomaterials is a fair description.

s04.note: Survival strategies under oxygen deprivation in vertebrates, assigned Molecular Biology through the topic Mitochondrial Function and Pathology. The work is comparative physiology. Physiology would describe it better, though the molecular framing is not absurd.

s05.note: Two-proton halo character of neon-17, assigned Nuclear and High Energy Physics. Exactly right.

s06.note: Temporal variation of coastal marine environmental DNA, assigned Ecology. Right.

s07.note: Microbial methanation in hybrid electric and biological anaerobic digestion, assigned Environmental Engineering. Right.

s08.note: Hydration friction at ionic interfaces probed at the atomic scale, assigned Atomic and Molecular Physics and Optics through a force microscopy topic. The work is nanoscale surface science; Condensed Matter Physics would fit better. In the right neighbourhood but not the right label.

s09.note: Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation, assigned Molecular Biology. A computational biology label would be sharper, but Molecular Biology is defensible for a metagenomics benchmark.

s10.note: Rydberg exciton polaritons in a cuprous oxide microcavity, assigned Atomic and Molecular Physics and Optics. Right.

s11.note: The euroSciVoc term electric power generation, matched two levels up on electrical engineering, was assigned the subfield Atomic and Molecular Physics and Optics. Electrical engineering should reach Electrical and Electronic Engineering. The keyword route sent it somewhere unrelated.

s12.note: biocatalysis matched one level up on catalysis and assigned the subfield Catalysis. Correct, and the climb costs nothing here.

s13.note: hydrocarbons matched one level up on organic chemistry and assigned Organic Chemistry. Correct.

s14.note: ecosystems matched one level up on ecology and assigned Ecology. Correct.

s15.note: The term coal, under fossil energy, matched exactly as a topic keyword and was assigned Mechanical Engineering. Coal belongs with fuel or energy technology. An exact leaf match through the keyword route is still wrong, which shows that the climb distance is not what makes a match unreliable.

s16.note: mobile phones, under telecommunications, assigned Information Systems. Computer Networks and Communications, or Electrical and Electronic Engineering, would be closer. Adjacent rather than correct.

s17.note: hydroelectricity climbed three levels to environmental engineering and was assigned Environmental Engineering. The euroSciVoc path really does place it there, so the mapping is faithful, but three levels of climb throws away everything specific about hydropower.

s18.note: atmospheric turbulence, a meteorology term, was assigned Atomic and Molecular Physics and Optics. The phrase is a keyword on free space optics topics, so the keyword route matched the wrong sense of the words.

s19.note: cryptography, under computer security, was assigned Artificial Intelligence. A clear miss; cryptography is not AI. The keyword route again.

s20.note: molecular neuroscience matched one level up on molecular biology and assigned Molecular Biology. Correct.

offline_check_against_natural_sciences_c.match_rule: a shared word of at least four characters that appears in fewer than five Danish organisation names in the corpus
offline_check_against_natural_sciences_c.distinctive_word_threshold: appears in fewer than 5 of 762 organisation names
offline_check_against_natural_sciences_c.caveat: matched on name tokens, so each finding should be read before it is believed. A miss is not evidence of no contact.

falsification_spotcheck.what_this_is: an attempt to disprove the not-yet-connected claims in data/actions.json using a source CORDIS cannot see
falsification_spotcheck.method: sample for-profit Danish organisations that the ranked list says share no Horizon Europe project with AU on that topic, resolve each to an OpenAlex institution by name, and count works co-authored by that institution and Aarhus University I204337017
falsification_spotcheck.name_matching_caveat: a name match is used here and nowhere else. It is sound in one direction only: a hit disproves the claim under test, a miss proves nothing because the name may simply not have resolved. Matched names are listed so a bad match can be spotted and discarded.

top_candidates_already_collaborating.note: a shared Horizon Europe project is the only kind of existing collaboration this can see; two organisations can work together through contract research, Innovation Fund Denmark, a student project or a consultancy and leave no trace in CORDIS, so this is a floor on existing collaboration and never a ceiling
